transcript.text: roomba e5 wont charge properly, sometimes it does sometimes it doesnt

Charging that works some days and not others on a robot vacuum is usually a contact problem rather than a dead part. Here are the likely causes, most likely first: - Dirty charging contacts. Dust, hair or a film builds up on the metal pads under the robot and on the dock, so contact comes and goes.
• The robot not seating properly on the dock. This happens if the dock is on carpet, a slope or in a cramped spot, so it lands slightly off-centre some of the time.
• An ageing battery. Roomba batteries typically start to struggle after two or three years, giving short run times, failing to take charge or charging errors.
• Less often, the dock's power lead, its socket, or a timer or switched socket. These checks will help tell them apart: 1. Clean the contacts. Unplug the dock first. Under the robot there are usually two metal charging pads, and the dock has two matching contacts. Wipe all of them with a dry cloth, or a cloth barely dampened with a little rubbing alcohol, then let them dry fully. If charging becomes reliable afterwards, dirt was the cause.
2. Check where the dock sits. It should be on a hard, level floor, flat against a wall, with roughly half a metre clear either side and more space in front. It should also be plugged into a socket that isn't on a timer or switched off at night. If moving it fixes things, it was a docking problem.
3. Place it on by hand. Put the robot squarely on the dock yourself and check it shows it's charging, with a light or a tone, or in the app. If it charges reliably by hand but not when it returns by itself, the problem is docking. If it still fails when seated by hand on clean contacts, suspect the battery or the dock.
4. Think about battery age and run time. If it's a few years old and the cleaning time has been getting shorter, the battery is the front runner. If it still won't charge reliably after all that, the battery is the usual culprit, with the dock as the next suspect. We can narrow it down once we know how it behaves on the hand test.
ok, app says Charging error 5 and the ring goes red. dock is on carpet by the sofa, a bit wonky. will try cleaning the contacts

Cleaning the contacts is a good first move. On Charging error 5, I can't confirm exactly what that code means on the e5 from the information I have, so I won't guess. In the iRobot app, tapping the error usually brings up iRobot's own explanation and steps, and that's worth a look. The dock position stands out. A dock on carpet that sits a bit wonky is one of the commonest reasons a Roomba charges some days and not others. The carpet lets the dock tilt or shift, and the robot can land slightly off its contacts. 1. Move the dock. Put it on a hard, level floor, flat against the wall, with clear space either side and in front, and keep it away from the sofa if the robot has to squeeze in. If the error stops after this, it was a docking problem.
2. Hand test. If it charges normally, the robot and battery are probably fine and positioning was the issue.
3. If the red ring and Charging error 5 come back even when it's seated by hand on clean contacts, the battery becomes the main suspect, especially if the robot is a few years old or its run time has been getting shorter. The dock is the next suspect after that. Let me know how it does on the hand test and roughly how old the robot is, and we can narrow it down from there.
cleaned the contacts, they had a greasy film and lots of hair. charged every night for 4 days now, no error. robot is about 4 years old. no heat or smell from it

That's sorted, then. No heat or smell is reassuring too. 1. Wipe the robot's charging pads and the dock contacts with a dry cloth every few weeks. Unplug the dock first. If the film returns, use a cloth barely dampened with rubbing alcohol.
2. If you can, move the dock off the carpet onto a hard, level floor, flat against the wall. A wonky dock was probably making the dirty contacts worse, and it can cause the same trouble again. One thing to keep an eye on: at about four years old, the battery is getting towards the age when they start to fade. If run times get noticeably shorter, or charging errors come back even with clean contacts and a level dock, a replacement battery is the likely next step. Is there anything else I can help with?
